metadata.title: Machine learning investigation of optimal psychoemotional well-being factors for students’ reading literacy

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The study uses PISA 2018 public microdata for the B-S-J-Z (China) region subset and constructs a student-level analytic dataset by excluding rows with missing values. The manuscript does not report applying PISA sampling weights or any replicate-weight scheme, and it does not name any weight variables from the PISA data. Because the analysis is a machine-learning classification pipeline (SVM with RFE-CV) implemented in Python/scikit-learn, the authors do not describe any complex-survey-weight adjustments for the nested sampling design (students within schools within regions). Analysts using the PISA microdata should consider whether to apply the official PISA student/sampling weights (and replicate weights if available) when estimating population-representative performance, but this paper’s reported accuracy appears to be based on unweighted preprocessing and train/test splitting.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Used the PISA 2018 public dataset and restricted to the B-S-J-Z (Beijing, Shanghai, Jiangsu, Zhejiang) region subset. The dependent variable was constructed from PISA reading plausible values by selecting plausible value 1 (PV1) for reading for each student. Students were then classified into high-level reading literacy (Level 5 and above; score cut-off 625.61) vs low-level reading literacy (Level 2 and below; score cut-off 407.47). The analytic sample was reduced from 12,058 participants in B-S-J-Z to 3,497 after excluding rows with missing values or invalid data (drop rows with missing values using Stata 'drop if missing()').

main_findings.target_variable: High vs low reading literacy (binary; Level 5+ vs Level 2-)
main_findings.performance_metrics: Model comparison: SVM (RBF) accuracy 0.90 (training) and 0.871 (test). Feature-set optimization: peak accuracy 0.905 when using 15 features (SVM-RFECV; cross-validation folds 10 or 13; highest CV accuracy 0.891).
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using PISA 2018 Reading (PV1) data for the B-S-J-Z (China) subset, the study leveraged socioeconomic status (ESCS), meaning in life (EUDMO), learning goals (MASTGOAL), disciplinary climate (DISCLIMA), and parents’ emotional support (EMOSUPS) to predict high vs low reading literacy, finding that the SVM classifier achieved 0.871 test accuracy and that a 15-factor psychoemotional well-being set reached a peak accuracy of 0.905. This indicates that targeted psychoemotional and school-climate supports—especially those linked to students’ socioeconomic context and motivational/meaning-related factors—may improve the identification of students at risk of low reading performance, though the results are predictive and not causal.

data.outcome_summary: The study analyzes PISA 2018 reading literacy for students in the B-S-J-Z (Beijing, Shanghai, Jiangsu, Zhejiang) subset of China, using PV1 as the reading plausible value and converting reading performance into a binary outcome (high: Level 5+; low: Level 2-). After excluding missing/invalid cases, the analytic sample contains 3,497 students (2,935 high-level and 562 low-level). The authors compare multiple ML classifiers and select an SVM with an RBF kernel, using RFE-CV with cross-validation folds ranging from 5 to 15 and evaluating performance primarily via accuracy. The best SVM achieved 0.90 training accuracy and 0.871 test accuracy, while the optimized 15-feature set reached a peak accuracy of 0.905. SHAP is used for interpretability (feature importance), but SHAP-based importance is not causal evidence, and the manuscript does not report the use of PISA sampling/replicate weights.
